classification.difficultyReason: Apply successive leading-term division with quadratic and cubic divisors and express each result as a division identity.

content.prompt: Divide $P(x)$ by $D(x)$ in each case. Express each result in the form $P(x)=D(x)Q(x)+R(x)$.

answer.worked:
Successive leading-term divisions give $x^3\div x^2=x$ and $4x^2\div x^2=4$. Subtract each multiple of the divisor:
$$\begin{align*}(x^3+5x^2-x+2)-x(x^2+x+1)&=4x^2-2x+2\\(4x^2-2x+2)-4(x^2+x+1)&=-6x-2.
\end{align*}$$
Thus $Q(x)=x+4$ and $R(x)=-6x-2$. The remainder has degree less than 2.
$$x^3+5x^2-x+2=(x^2+x+1)(x+4)-6x-2.$$

Successive leading-term divisions give $x^3\div x^2=x$ and $-2x^2\div x^2=-2$. Subtract each multiple of the divisor:
$$\begin{align*}(x^3-4x^2-3x+7)-x(x^2-2x+3)&=-2x^2-6x+7\\(-2x^2-6x+7)-(-2)(x^2-2x+3)&=-10x+13.
\end{align*}$$
Thus $Q(x)=x-2$ and $R(x)=-10x+13$. The remainder has degree less than 2.
$$x^3-4x^2-3x+7=(x^2-2x+3)(x-2)-10x+13.$$

Include zero coefficients for the missing powers. Successive leading-term divisions give $x^2$, $3x$ and $17$. Subtract each multiple of the divisor:
$$\begin{align*}(x^4+0x^3+5x^2+0x+3)-x^2(x^2-3x-3)&=3x^3+8x^2+3\\(3x^3+8x^2+3)-3x(x^2-3x-3)&=17x^2+9x+3\\(17x^2+9x+3)-17(x^2-3x-3)&=60x+54.
\end{align*}$$
Thus $Q(x)=x^2+3x+17$ and $R(x)=60x+54$. The remainder has degree less than 2.
$$x^4+5x^2+3=(x^2-3x-3)(x^2+3x+17)+60x+54.$$

Include zero coefficients for the missing powers. Successive leading-term divisions give $x^2$, $-2x$ and $-3$. Subtract each multiple of the divisor:
$$\begin{align*}(x^5-3x^4+0x^3-9x^2+0x+9)-x^2(x^3-x^2+x-1)&=-2x^4-x^3-8x^2+9\\(-2x^4-x^3-8x^2+9)-(-2x)(x^3-x^2+x-1)&=-3x^3-6x^2-2x+9\\(-3x^3-6x^2-2x+9)-(-3)(x^3-x^2+x-1)&=-9x^2+x+6.
\end{align*}$$
Thus $Q(x)=x^2-2x-3$ and $R(x)=-9x^2+x+6$. The remainder has degree less than 3.
$$x^5-3x^4-9x^2+9=(x^3-x^2+x-1)(x^2-2x-3)-9x^2+x+6.$$
